request:
Our campus has a lost-and-found desk and we want a simple board for it. Anyone who finds something can report it with a short description of the item, where they found it and the date they found it. People should be able to see all the items on the board and look at one item. When the owner comes to collect an item, the desk marks it as claimed and writes down the owner's name. An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed again. We also want to see only the items that are still waiting for their owners.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Should only desk staff be able to mark an item as claimed (for example with a password), or can anyone using the board do it?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Should everyone be able to see the owner's name on claimed items, or should it be visible only to desk staff?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Should items ever be removed from the board, for example if no one claims them after a set number of days? If so, how many days?
A: No preference: you decide.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I've built the lost-and-found board in `app.py`, and all 10 of my tests pass. Items are saved in a file called `lost_and_found.db` in the project folder, which is created automatically when the app starts.

**Endpoints:**
- **POST /items**: reports a found item. It needs `description`, `found_where` and `found_on` (a date, for example `2024-05-01`). The system gives the item a number, marks it as waiting for its owner and leaves the owner's name empty. A report that is missing any of the three details, leaves one blank or has an invalid date is refused.
- **GET /items**: lists every item on the board, claimed and waiting.
- **GET /items/waiting**: lists only the items still waiting for their owners.
- **GET /items/{id}**: shows one item with all its details.
- **POST /items/{id}/claim**: takes `owner_name`, marks the item as claimed and records the name. A claim without a name is refused. If the item is already claimed, the claim is refused and the first owner's name stays unchanged.
- If you look up or claim an item number that doesn't exist, you get the message "Item not found".

As we agreed in the plan, I went with the simplest options. Anyone using the board can mark an item as claimed, and there are no passwords. The owner's name is shown with the item's other details. Items are never removed automatically.

plan.summary: This plan is for a simple lost-and-found board for your campus desk. Anyone who finds something can report it with a short description, the place it was found and the date it was found. Everyone can see the whole board, look at a single item, or see only the items still waiting for their owners. When an owner collects an item, the desk marks it as claimed and records the owner's name. An item that is already claimed cannot be claimed again. Since you had no preference on your three questions, we chose the simplest options: anyone using the board can mark an item as claimed (no passwords or staff accounts), the owner's name is shown on claimed items like the rest of the item's details, and items are never removed from the board automatically. Some questions for you to consider before we build: Would you like only desk staff to be able to mark items as claimed, so that someone cannot falsely claim an item through the board? Would you prefer to hide owners' names from the public for privacy? Would you like old unclaimed items to be removed after a certain number of days? None of these are included in this plan unless you ask for them.

data.name: Found item
fields: Item number (given automatically by the system so each item can be looked up)
Status: waiting for owner, or claimed (starts as waiting for owner)
Owner's name (empty until the item is claimed)

endpoints.does: Report a found item by giving a short description, where it was found and the date it was found. The item is added to the board as waiting for its owner.
Show all items on the board, both claimed and still waiting.
Show only the items that are still waiting for their owners.
Show one item and all its details.
Mark an item as claimed when the owner collects it, and write down the owner's name.

rules: A report must include a short description, where the item was found and the date it was found; a report missing any of these is refused.
Marking an item as claimed must include the owner's name; a claim without a name is refused.
An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed again; the attempt is refused and the original owner's name stays unchanged.
Looking up or claiming an item number that does not exist is refused with a message saying the item was not found.
